families.label: short -a masculine
families.note: Every -a masculine declines alike: deva, rāma, nara… Change the stem, no rule changes.

families.label: short -a neuter
families.note: Oblique cases match the masculine; nominative, accusative and vocative do not.

families.label: long -ā feminine
families.note: yā-ādeśa before vowel endings: sītayā, sītāyai, sītāyāḥ.

families.label: long -ī feminine
families.note: ī shortens to y before vowels: nadyā, nadyai, nadyāḥ.

families.label: long -ū feminine
families.note: ū shortens to v before vowels: vadhvā, vadhvai, vadhvāḥ.

families.label: -i masculine
families.note: New family: agninā, agnaye, agneḥ, agnau. Final i guṇates to e before ṅ-endings.

families.label: -i neuter
families.note: Neuter i-stems take -nā, -ne, -naḥ: vāriṇā, vāriṇe, vāriṇaḥ.

families.label: -u masculine
families.note: Like -i with its own vowel: guruṇā, gurave, guroḥ, gurau.

families.label: -ṛ agent noun
families.note: pitā, pitrā, pitre, pituḥ. Final ṛ is strong in the nominative.

families.label: -an masculine
families.note: rājā, rājñā, rājñe, rājñaḥ — the n assimilates before endings.

families.label: -c feminine
families.note: vāk, vācā, vāce, vācaḥ — the final stop devoices in the nominative.

families.label: -as neuter
families.note: manaḥ, manasā, manase, manasaḥ — s becomes ḥ in the nominative.

families.label: -in masculine
families.note: sukhī, sukhinā, sukhine — the in-stem that makes adjectives agree.

families.label: -ant participle
families.note: bhavan, bhavantā, bhavate — present participles decline like this.

families.label: -vant masculine
families.note: bhagavan, bhagavantā, bhagavate — the -vant possession suffix.

families.label: diphthong stem
families.note: go → gauḥ, gavā, gave, goḥ. Irregular but regular in its own pattern.

stems.note: same rules as deva — transfer test
